name: Axumite Empire
description: Ethiopian-Sabean kingdom. Aksum obelisks. Christianity state religion. Trade with India and Rome.

name: Nok Culture
description: Iron Age culture in Nigeria. Terracotta sculptures. Early ironworking in West Africa.

name: Ghana Empire
description: West African Sahelian empire. Gold trade. Koumbi Saleh capital. Almoravid pressure.

name: Mali Empire
description: West African empire. Mansa Musa's hajj. Timbuktu and Djenné. Gold trade. Songhai secession.

name: Songhai Empire
description: West African empire. Sunni Ali. Askia Muhammad. Timbuktu scholars. Moroccan invasion 1591.

name: Kanem-Bornu Empire
description: Sahelian empire. Horses and cavalry. Islamic scholarship. Mai Idris Alooma. Declined under Fulani and European pressure.

name: Benin Empire
description: Edo kingdom in Nigeria. Benin Bronzes. Oba monarchy. British punitive expedition 1897.

name: Oyo Empire
description: Yoruba empire. Cavalry. Dahomey rival. British protectorate. Collapsed in 19th century.

name: Dahomey Kingdom
description: Fon kingdom. Amazon warriors. Slave trade. French conquest.

name: Kingdom of Kongo
description: Central African kingdom. Manikongo. Christianity (state). Portuguese alliance. Declined under slave trade and Portuguese pressure.

name: Great Zimbabwe
description: Shona kingdom in Zimbabwe. Great Enclosure. Gold and ivory trade. Declined due to resource depletion.

name: Kingdom of Mutapa
description: Shona successor state. Portuguese trade. Declined due to civil wars and Portuguese pressure.

name: Ethiopian Empire
description: Solomonic dynasty. Lalibela churches. Italian occupation. Haile Selassie. Derg coup 1974.

name: Ashanti Empire
description: Akan empire in Ghana. Golden Stool. Osei Tutu. British wars. Annexation 1902.

name: Sokoto Caliphate
description: Fulani jihad state. Usman dan Fodio. Hausa city-states. British conquest.

name: Olmec Civilization
description: Mesoamerican mother culture. Colossal heads. La Venta. San Lorenzo. Undeciphered script.

name: Maya City-States
description: Classic Maya civilization. Tikal, Palenque, Copan. Calendar, writing, astronomy. Postclassic decline. Spanish conquest.

name: Teotihuacan
description: Mesoamerican mega-city. Pyramid of the Sun. Obsidian trade. Collapse and burning.

name: Toltec Culture
description: Postclassic Mesoamerican culture. Tula capital. Quetzalcoatl legend. Chichen Itza contact.

name: Aztec Empire
description: Triple Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, Tlacopan. Montezuma. Conquered by Cortes.

name: Mississippian Culture
description: Mound-builder culture. Cahokia. Maize agriculture. Chiefdoms. Hernando de Soto contact.

name: Inca Empire
description: Andean empire. Cuzco capital. Machu Picchu. Quipu. Road system. Conquered by Pizarro.

name: Chimor Kingdom
description: Chimu civilization. Chan Chan capital. Adobe cities. Conquered by Inca.

name: Muisca Confederation
description: Andean chiefdom confederation. El Dorado legend. Goldwork. Spanish conquest.

name: Viceroyalty of New Spain
description: Spanish colonial administration in Mexico, Central America, Caribbean, Philippines. Silver economy.
politics: Colonial viceroyalty with Council of Indies

name: Viceroyalty of Peru
description: Spanish colonial administration in Andes. Potosi silver. Lima capital. Bourbon reforms. Independence.
politics: Colonial viceroyalty with Council of Indies

name: Xiongnu Confederation
description: Steppe confederation. Rival of Han China. Modu Chanyu. Divided into Northern and Southern. Southern submitted to Han.

name: Scythian Cultures
description: Iranian steppe nomads. Gold art. Greek contact. Herodotus' account. Sarmatian successors.

name: Sarmatians
description: Iranian steppe nomads west of Scythians. Heavy cavalry. Roman frontier contact. Hunnic pressure ended dominance.

name: Yuezhi
description: Indo-European nomads driven west by Xiongnu. Became Kushans in South Asia. Gansu origins.

name: Hepthalite Empire
description: White Huns. Central Asian empire. Rival of Sassanids and Gupta. Overthrown by Sassanid-Turk alliance.

name: Gokturk Khaganate
description: First Turkic empire. Orkhon inscriptions. Rival of Sui and Tang. Split into Eastern and Western. Uyghur overthrow.

name: Uyghur Khaganate
description: Turkic empire replacing Gokturks. Manichaeism state religion. Fell to Kyrgyz.

name: Khazar Khaganate
description: Turkic state between Black and Caspian Seas. Judaism elite religion (possibly). Rival of Arab caliphates and Rus. Kievan Rus overthrow.

name: Kara-Khanid Khanate
description: Turkic state in Central Asia. Islam state religion. Kashgar capital. Qarakhanid law. Qara Khitai overthrow.

name: Khwarazmian Empire
description: Persianate state in Central Asia. Anushtegin dynasty. Destroyed by Genghis Khan.

name: Mongol Empire
description: Largest contiguous land empire. Genghis Khan. Pax Mongolica. Yasa code. Divided into khanates.

name: Chagatai Khanate
description: Central Asian successor khanate. Bukhara and Samarkand. Timurid overthrow in west. Dzungar conquest in east.

name: Golden Horde
description: Mongol successor state in Russia and steppe. Sarai capital. Islamized. Moscow princes as tribute collectors.

name: Timurid Empire
description: Turko-Mongol empire of Tamerlane. Samarkand capital. Cultural renaissance. Fragmented after Timur's death.

name: Uzbek Khanates
description: Shaybanid and later Uzbek states in Central Asia. Bukhara, Khiva, Kokand. Russian conquest.

name: Dzungar Khanate
description: Oirat Mongol state in Dzungaria. Rival of Qing. Buddhism (Gelug). Qing conquest.

name: Siberian Khanate
description: Tatar state in western Siberia. Kuchum Khan. Yermak conquest 1582. Russian annexation.

name: Xia Dynasty (conventional chronology)
description: First traditionally attested Chinese dynasty. Archaeological confirmation remains incomplete; dates follow the Xia-Shang-Zhou Chronology Project conventional framework. Capitals possibly at Erlitou and other Henan sites.
religion: Ancestral cult, shamanism, early Tian cosmology

name: Shang Dynasty
description: First Chinese dynasty with direct archaeological evidence (Anyang oracle bones, bronze ritual vessels). Warrior-aristocracy with divination-centered court ritual. Multiple capitals including Yin (Anyang).
religion: Shangdi worship, ancestor veneration, oracle-bone divination

name: Western Zhou
description: Mandate of Heaven concept developed. Feudal enfeoffment system with royal domain in Guanzhong and regional states across North China Plain. Collapsed after Quanrong invasion.
politics: Feudal kingship with enfeoffed regional lords

name: Eastern Zhou
description: Royal house moved to Luoyang; real power devolved to regional states. Period encompasses both Spring & Autumn and Warring States sub-periods. Zhou king became largely ceremonial.
religion: Confucian and Daoist thought emerging, ancestral rites
politics: Nominal kingship with de facto independent regional states

name: Spring & Autumn Period
description: Sub-period of Eastern Zhou characterized by interstate warfare among major states (Qi, Jin, Chu, Qin, Lu). Confucius lived during this era. Hegemon (ba) system maintained nominal Zhou legitimacy.
religion: Zhou ancestral cult, emerging philosophical schools

name: Warring States Period
description: Intensified warfare among seven major powers. Legalist reforms in Qin, Mohist and Daoist philosophical flourishing. Mass infantry armies replaced chariot aristocracy. Qin eventually conquered all rivals.

name: Qin Dynasty
description: First unified imperial regime in Chinese history. Standardized weights, measures, script, and coinage. Massive public works including Great Wall precursor and Epang Palace. Collapsed rapidly after First Emperor's death.
religion: Legalist state ideology, suppression of rival schools

name: Western Han
description: Long-lived stable empire with Confucianism as state orthodoxy. Expansion into Central Asia, Korea, and Vietnam. Silk Road opened. Civil service examination precursors established.
religion: Confucian state orthodoxy, syncretic Huang-Lao early

name: Xin Dynasty
description: Wang Mang's short-lived interregnum between Western and Eastern Han. Attempted radical land redistribution and currency reform. Peasant rebellions (Red Eyebrows, Green Woodsmen) destroyed the regime.

name: Eastern Han
description: Capital moved to Luoyang. Eunuch and consort clan factions weakened the court. Yellow Turban rebellion (184) devastated the realm. Warlordism ended the dynasty.
politics: Monarchy with eunuch and consort clan factions

name: Cao Wei
description: One of the Three Kingdoms. Controlled the Central Plains and northern China. Cao Cao and Cao Pi established bureaucratic reforms but faced Shu and Wu coalitions.
politics: Bureaucratic monarchy with military strongman origins

name: Shu Han
description: Liu Bei founded this kingdom in Sichuan. Zhuge Liang's campaigns against Wei and administrative reforms. Conquered by Wei in 263.
politics: Bureaucratic monarchy with military strongman origins

name: Eastern Wu
description: Sun Quan founded this southern kingdom. Controlled the Yangtze basin and extended into Jiaozhi (Vietnam). Maritime trade with Southeast Asia.
politics: Bureaucratic monarchy with military strongman origins

name: Western Jin
description: Brief reunification after Three Kingdoms. Sima clan ruled but court intrigue and the War of the Eight Princes weakened the state. Xiongnu and other groups overran the north.
politics: Bureaucratic monarchy with powerful aristocratic clans

name: Eastern Jin
description: Chinese court in exile at Jiankang (Nanjing). Ruled south China while north was under non-Han dynasties. Aristocratic clans dominated politics. Buddhism spread significantly.
religion: Buddhism expansion, Daoism, Confucian elite culture
politics: Weak monarchy with aristocratic clan coalitions
majorEvents: Sima Rui establishes court at Jiankang

name: Northern Wei
description: Xianbei-ruled dynasty that unified northern China. Sinicization policies under Emperor Xiaowen (Luoyang relocation, clothing/language reforms). Buddhist cave temples at Yungang and Longmen.
politics: Xianbei military aristocracy with Chinese bureaucracy

name: Liu Song
description: First of the Southern Dynasties. Founded by Liu Yu, a military strongman. Brief northern campaigns but generally defensive against Northern Wei.

name: Southern Qi
description: Short-lived southern dynasty. Founded by Xiao Daocheng. Literary culture flourished but court intrigue was rampant.

name: Liang Dynasty
description: Founded by Xiao Yan. Emperor Wu was a devout Buddhist who monastically donated himself to temples. Hou Jing rebellion devastated the realm.

name: Chen Dynasty
description: Last of the Southern Dynasties. Founded by Chen Baxian. Controlled only the southeastern core after Liang's collapse. Conquered by Sui in 589.
majorEvents: Loss of Sichuan to Western Wei

name: Sui Dynasty
description: Reunified China after nearly three centuries of division. Built the Grand Canal, expanded the Great Wall, and restored centralized administration. Overextension in Korea and massive conscription triggered collapse.

name: Tang Dynasty
description: Golden age of Chinese civilization. Cosmopolitan empire stretching to Central Asia and Korea. Poetry, printing, and civil service examination flourished. An Lushan rebellion (755-763) marked the turning point.

name: Later Liang
description: First of the Five Dynasties. Founded by Zhu Wen, a former Huang Chao rebel. Controlled the Central Plains but faced rival states.

name: Later Tang
description: Second of the Five Dynasties. Founded by Li Cunxu, ethnically Shatuo Turk. Claimed Tang restoration. Conquered by Later Jin.

name: Later Jin
description: Third of the Five Dynasties. Ceded Sixteen Prefectures to Liao. Founded by Shi Jingtang with Khitan support.
politics: Military strongman monarchy with Liao suzerainty

name: Later Han
description: Fourth of the Five Dynasties. Very short-lived. Founded by Liu Zhiyuan. Collapsed due to regicide.

name: Later Zhou
description: Last of the Five Dynasties. Founded by Guo Wei. Chai Rong's reforms and campaigns set the stage for Song unification.

name: Wu Yue
description: Ten Kingdoms state in Zhejiang. Founded by Qian Liu. Maritime trade and cultural development. Peacefully submitted to Song.

name: Southern Tang
description: Ten Kingdoms state in lower Yangtze. Cultural renaissance under Li Yu's court. Conquered by Song.

name: Northern Song
description: Reunified most of China proper. Civil service examination peak, commercial revolution, and neo-Confucianism. Lost north to Jin in 1127.
politics: Centralized bureaucracy with weak military command

name: Western Xia
description: Tangut-ruled state in northwest China. Created Tangut script. Militant Buddhist state. Conquered by Mongols under Genghis Khan.

name: Southern Song
description: Song court in exile at Lin'an (Hangzhou). Maritime trade and technological innovation reached new heights. Neo-Confucianism matured. Fell to Yuan.

name: Liao Dynasty
description: Khitan-ruled empire in Mongolia, Manchuria, and north China. Dual administration system for Khitan and Han subjects. Buddhism state religion.
politics: Dual Khitan-Han administration with seasonal migrations

name: Jin Dynasty (Jurchen)
description: Jurchen-ruled dynasty that conquered Liao and Northern Song. Controlled north China. Overthrown by Mongols and Southern Song alliance.

name: Yuan Dynasty
description: Mongol-ruled dynasty over all China. First foreign dynasty to rule all of China. Kubilai Khan established Dadu (Beijing). Pax Mongolica facilitated Eurasian trade.
politics: Mongol military aristocracy with Chinese bureaucracy

name: Ming Dynasty
description: Han Chinese restoration after Mongol rule. Autocratic emperor system with eunuch and civil service factions. Zheng He's voyages, Great Wall rebuilding, and porcelain export economy.
politics: Autocratic monarchy with civil service and eunuch factions

name: Qing Dynasty
description: Manchu-ruled dynasty. Conquered Ming and expanded to include Tibet, Xinjiang, Mongolia, and Taiwan. High Qing (Kangxi, Yongzheng, Qianlong) was prosperous; 19th century saw Opium Wars and rebellions.
politics: Manchu military aristocracy with Chinese civil service

name: Republic of China
description: Post-imperial republic. Warlord era, Nationalist unification under Chiang Kai-shek, Japanese invasion, and civil war with Communists. Government retreated to Taiwan in 1949.
politics: Parliamentary republic to one-party Nationalist state
majorEvents: Civil war and retreat to Taiwan

name: People's Republic of China
description: Communist state founded by Mao Zedong. Land reform, Great Leap Forward, Cultural Revolution, Reform and Opening since 1978, and rapid industrialization. World's second-largest economy.
religion: State atheism, religious freedom constitutionally guaranteed

name: Goguryeo
description: Korean kingdom controlling Manchuria and northern Korea. Major power in Northeast Asia. Buddhism and Daoism flourished. Fell to Silla-Tang alliance.

name: Silla
description: Korean kingdom that unified the peninsula in 668. Bone-rank system. Maritime trade with Tang China. Bulguksa temple and Seokguram grotto.

name: Baekje
description: Korean kingdom in southwest Korea. Maritime culture with strong ties to Japan and China. Conqued by Tang-Silla alliance.

name: Joseon Dynasty
description: Neo-Confucian Korean state. Hangul alphabet created. Turtle ships. Hermit kingdom policy in 19th century. Fell to Japanese annexation.

name: Korean Empire
description: Short-lived empire proclaimed by Gojong to assert independence from Qing. Modernizing reforms. Annexed by Japan in 1910.

name: Yamato Japan
description: Emerging Japanese state centered in Kansai. Uji clan system. Buddhism introduced from Korea and China. Taika Reform (645) and Ritsuryo system.

name: Heian Japan
description: Aristocratic court culture at Kyoto. Fujiwara regency. Tale of Genji. Rise of samurai class. Genpei War ended the era.

name: Kamakura Shogunate
description: First samurai government. Minamoto no Yoritomo as shogun. Mongol invasions repelled. Hojo regency eventually collapsed.

name: Muromachi Shogunate
description: Ashikaga shogunate. Onin War devastated Kyoto. Sengoku daimyo period. Tea culture and Noh theater. Portuguese arrival 1543.

name: Tokugawa Shogunate
description: Centralized feudalism under Tokugawa Ieyasu. 250 years of peace (Pax Tokugawa). Sakoku isolation policy. Urban culture and ukiyo-e.

name: Empire of Japan
description: Modernizing empire under Meiji Constitution. Industrialization, colonial expansion (Taiwan, Korea, Manchuria), Pacific War. Dissolved under US occupation.

name: Hunnic Empire
description: Steppe confederation. Attila. Invasions of Europe. Collapsed after Attila's death.

name: Avar Khaganate
description: Eurasian steppe empire in Pannonia. Byzantine tribute. Charlemagne conquest.

name: Tu'i Tonga Empire
description: Tongan maritime empire in Polynesia. Sacred kingship. Influence over Samoa, Fiji, Niue.

name: Classical Greece
description: City-state culture (Athens, Sparta). Democracy, philosophy, tragedy. Peloponnesian War. Conquered by Macedonia.

name: Macedonian Empire
description: Northern Greek kingdom. Philip II unified Greece. Alexander conquered Persia. Divided into successor states.

name: Carolingian Empire
description: Frankish empire under Charlemagne. Renaissance of learning. Aachen capital. Treaty of Verdun divided it.

name: Frankish Kingdom
description: Merovingian and Carolingian rule in Gaul. Clovis' conversion. Expansion under Charlemagne. Divided by Treaty of Verdun.

name: Visigothic Kingdom
description: Germanic kingdom in Spain and Gaul. Arian then Catholic. Toledo capital. Islamic conquest 711.

name: Ostrogothic Kingdom
description: Theodoric's kingdom in Italy. Preserved Roman administration. Justinian's Gothic Wars destroyed it.

name: Vandal Kingdom
description: Germanic kingdom in North Africa. Arian Christianity. Sacked Rome 455. Belisarius reconquered it.

name: Anglo-Saxon Heptarchy
description: Seven kingdoms in England. Bede. Conversion to Christianity. Viking invasions. Alfred the Great. Unified by Athelstan.

name: Holy Roman Empire
description: Germanic empire claiming Roman continuity. Habsburg dominance from 1438. Thirty Years' War. Dissolved by Napoleon.

name: Kingdom of England
description: Unified English kingdom. Magna Carta. Hundred Years' War. Reformation. Spanish Armada. Civil War. Union with Scotland.

name: Angevin Empire
description: Plantagenet domains in England and France. Henry II and Eleanor. Magna Carta. Lost most French territories.

name: Kingdom of Jerusalem
description: Crusader state in the Levant. Baldwin I. Saladin's reconquest 1187. Third Crusade. Acre fell 1291.

name: Teutonic Knights State
description: German military order state in Prussia and Baltic. Converted pagans. Grunwald 1410. Secularized by Albert of Prussia.

name: Habsburg Monarchy
description: Habsburg dynastic composite state. Austria, Hungary, Bohemia, Netherlands, Spain (until 1700). Counter-Reformation.

name: Spanish Habsburg Empire
description: Global monarchy under Habsburgs. American colonies. Armada 1588. Declined after Thirty Years' War.

name: Bourbon Spain
description: French Bourbon dynasty in Spain. Enlightened despotism. American independence movements. Napoleonic invasion.

name: Portuguese Empire
description: First global maritime empire. Age of Discoveries. Brazil, Africa, Asia. Decolonization in 1970s.

name: Dutch Republic
description: Protestant maritime republic. Golden Age. VOC and WIC. Rembrandt. Anglo-Dutch wars. Patriot Revolution.

name: British Empire
description: Largest empire in history. Industrial revolution. Parliamentary democracy. World Wars. Decolonization.

name: French Empire (Napoleonic)
description: Napoleon Bonaparte's empire. Continental System. Napoleonic Code. Invasion of Russia. Waterloo.

name: Kingdom of France
description: Medieval and early modern France. Capetians. Hundred Years' War. Louis XIV. Enlightenment. Revolution.

name: Swedish Empire
description: Baltic great power under Gustavus Adolphus. Thirty Years' War. Great Northern War ended dominance.

name: Venetian Republic
description: Maritime merchant republic. St. Mark's. Arsenal. Mediterranean trade. Declined with New World routes. Napoleon ended it.

name: Russian Empire
description: Romanov dynasty empire. Peter the Great westernization. Catherine the Great. Siberian expansion. Napoleonic Wars. Revolution.

name: Soviet Union
description: Communist superpower. Industrialization. WWII. Cold War. Space race. Collapsed 1991.

name: Austro-Hungarian Empire
description: Dual monarchy of Austria and Hungary. Franz Joseph. Balkan tensions. WWI collapse.

name: German Empire
description: Prussian-led unified Germany. Bismarck. Industrial powerhouse. WWI. Weimar transition.

name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
description: Dual republic of Poland and Lithuania. Golden Liberty. Elective monarchy. Partitioned by Russia, Prussia, Austria.

name: Kalmar Union
description: Personal union of Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. Margrethe I. Swedish independence under Gustav Vasa.

name: Danish Empire
description: Denmark-Norway and colonial holdings. Christian IV. Thirty Years' War. Absolute monarchy. Norway lost 1814.

name: Swiss Confederation
description: Medieval alliance of cantons. Neutrality. Direct democracy. Banking. Multilingual.

name: Italian City-States
description: Florence, Venice, Milan, Genoa, Papal States. Renaissance. Medici. Maritime republics. Italian Wars.

name: Old Kingdom Egypt
description: Pyramid Age. Djoser step pyramid, Giza pyramids. Divine kingship. Collapsed into First Intermediate Period.

name: Middle Kingdom Egypt
description: Reunification under Mentuhotep II. Expansion into Nubia. Literature flourished. Hyksos invasion ended it.

name: New Kingdom Egypt
description: Imperial Egypt. Valley of the Kings. Akhenaten's monotheism. Tutankhamun. Ramesses II. Sea Peoples invasions.

name: Ptolemaic Kingdom
description: Hellenistic Egyptian kingdom. Alexandria Library. Cleopatra VII. Roman annexation after Actium.

name: Minoan Civilization
description: Bronze Age Aegean civilization. Knossos palace. Linear A script (undeciphered). Thera eruption contributed to decline.

name: Mycenaean Greece
description: Bronze Age Greek civilization. Linear B script. Trojan War legends. Palace system collapse around 1100 BCE.

name: Phoenicia
description: Levantine maritime traders. Alphabet invention. Carthage and other colonies. Tyre, Sidon, Byblos city-states.

name: Kingdom of Kush
description: Nubian kingdom south of Egypt. Napata and Meroe capitals. Pyramids at Meroe. Egyptian cultural influence.

name: Carthaginian Empire
description: Phoenician colony that became Mediterranean power. Hannibal's Alpine crossing. Punic Wars with Rome. Destroyed in Third Punic War.

name: Roman Republic
description: Senatorial oligarchy. Punic Wars. Marian reforms. Civil wars. Transition to Principate under Augustus.

name: Roman Empire
description: Pax Romana. Roman law, roads, and aqueducts. Christianity legalized. Division into East and West. Western collapse 476 CE.

name: Western Roman Empire
description: Western half of divided Roman Empire. Barbarian generals dominated. Romulus Augustulus deposed 476. Formal end of ancient Rome.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: Eastern Roman Empire. Constantinople. Justinian's law code. Iconoclasm. Macedonian Renaissance. Fell to Ottomans.

name: Fatimid Caliphate
description: Ismaili Shiite caliphate. Cairo capital. Al-Azhar University. Crusades began during their decline.

name: Ayyubid Dynasty
description: Saladin's dynasty. Defeated Crusaders at Hattin 1187. Jerusalem recaptured. Mamluk overthrow.

name: Mamluk Sultanate
description: Turkic and Circassian military slave dynasty ruling Egypt and Syria. Defeated Mongols at Ain Jalut 1260. Ottoman conquest.

name: Almoravid Empire
description: Berber Islamic reform movement controlling Morocco and Spain. Ibn Tumart opposition led to Almohads.

name: Almohad Caliphate
description: Berber Islamic empire. Ibn Tumart's mahdist movement. Averroes. Declined after Las Navas de Tolosa 1212.

name: Saadi Dynasty
description: Moroccan dynasty resisting Portuguese and Ottoman expansion. Battle of Ksar el Kebir 1578. Declined after Ahmad al-Mansur.

name: Moroccan Alaouite Dynasty
description: Current Moroccan ruling dynasty. Moulay Ismail's Black Guard. French and Spanish protectorates. Independence 1956.

name: Sumer
description: World's earliest civilization. City-states (Uruk, Ur, Lagash). Cuneiform writing. Ziggurats. Sargon of Akkad conquered it.

name: Akkadian Empire
description: First empire in Mesopotamia. Sargon of Akkad unified Sumer and Akkad. Spread Akkadian language. Collapsed due to Gutian invasions and climate change.

name: Old Babylonian Empire
description: Hammurabi's law code. Marduk cult. Amorite dynasty. Hittite sack of Babylon ended the era.

name: Middle Babylonian Empire
description: Kassite dynasty. Babylonian Dark Age relative to Assyria. Dur-Kurigalzu. Maintained cultural continuity.

name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
description: Chaldean dynasty. Nebuchadnezzar's Hanging Gardens. Babylonian captivity of Jews. Conquered by Cyrus the Great.

name: Old Assyrian Empire
description: Early Assyrian state in Upper Mesopotamia. Karum trade colonies in Anatolia. Shamshi-Adad I expansion.

name: Middle Assyrian Empire
description: Assyrian resurgence after Mitanni. Tiglath-Pileser I campaigns. Legal code. Aramean pressure weakened the state.

name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
description: Largest Mesopotamian empire. Professional army, deportations, and libraries (Ashurbanipal). Fell to Medes and Babylonians.

name: Hittite Empire
description: Anatolian empire. First ironworking. Hattusa capital. Kadesh battle with Egypt. Sea Peoples invasion ended it.

name: Mitanni
description: Hurrian-ruled state in Syria and Upper Mesopotamia. Chariot warfare. Diplomatic archive at Amarna.

name: Urartu
description: Iron Age kingdom in Armenia and eastern Anatolia. Fortress architecture. Rival of Assyria. Conquered by Medes.

name: Median Empire
description: First Iranian empire. Unifier of Iranian plateau. Herodotus' account. Conquered by Cyrus the Great.

name: Achaemenid Empire
description: First Persian empire. Cyrus the Great to Darius III. Royal Road. Persepolis. Conquered by Alexander the Great.

name: Seleucid Empire
description: Hellenistic successor state to Alexander's Asian conquests. Antioch capital. Silk Road trade. Roman and Parthian pressure.

name: Parthian Empire
description: Iranian empire reviving Persian traditions. Ctesiphon capital. Crassus defeat at Carrhae. Silk Road intermediaries.

name: Sassanid Empire
description: Neo-Persian empire. Zoroastrian state church. Ctesiphon. Khosrow I reforms. Fell to Arab Muslims.
politics: Centralized monarchy with noble and priestly estates

name: Umayyad Caliphate
description: First Islamic caliphate dynasty. Damascus capital. Expansion to Spain and Central Asia. Abbasid revolution overthrew it.
politics: Arab tribal monarchy with provincial governors

name: Abbasid Caliphate
description: Golden age of Islam. Baghdad capital. House of Wisdom. Harun al-Rashid. Mongol sack of Baghdad ended the caliphate.
politics: Bureaucratic monarchy with Turkish military slaves

name: Buyid Dynasty
description: Shiite Iranian dynasty controlling Baghdad and caliphs. Iraqi and Iranian core. Seljuk overthrow.

name: Seljuk Empire
description: Turko-Persian Sunni empire. Alp Arslan; Manzikert 1071. Sultanate of Rum branch. Khwarazmian overthrow.

name: Ilkhanate
description: Mongol successor state in Iran and Middle East. Ghazan conversion to Islam. Rashid al-Din historiography. Fragmented after Abu Said.

name: Safavid Empire
description: Shiite Iranian empire. Isfahan capital. Shah Abbas I. Qizilbash military. Declined after Abbas I.

name: Qajar Dynasty
description: Turkic dynasty ruling Iran. Constitutional Revolution 1906. Tobacco protest. British and Russian spheres of influence.

name: Ottoman Empire
description: Turkish empire spanning three continents. Constantinople 1453. Suleiman the Magnificent. Millet system. Declined in 19th century.

name: Indus Valley Civilization
description: One of the world's earliest urban cultures. Harappa and Mohenjo-daro. Undeciphered script. Declined due to climate change and Aryan migrations.

name: Maurya Empire
description: First pan-Indian empire. Chandragupta overthrew Nanda dynasty. Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism after Kalinga War. Rock edicts.

name: Kushan Empire
description: Central Asian empire controlling northwest India and Central Asia trade routes. Gandharan art. Kanishka's Buddhist council.

name: Gupta Empire
description: Golden age of classical India. Kalidasa, decimal numeral system, concept of zero. Hindu temple architecture. Huna invasions ended the era.

name: Harsha Empire
description: Short-lived north Indian empire. Harsha Vardhana was a patron of Buddhism and culture. Xuanzang visited his court.

name: Chalukya Empire
description: Deccan-based empire. Badami cave temples. Rashtrakuta overthrow. Rivalry with Pallavas.

name: Rashtrakuta Empire
description: Deccan empire controlling much of India. Ellora Kailasa temple. Rivalry with Pratiharas and Palas.

name: Pala Empire
description: Bengal-based empire. Buddhist university of Nalanda and Vikramashila patronage. Rivalry with Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas.

name: Chola Empire
description: Tamil maritime empire. Brihadeeswarar temple. Indian Ocean trade. Naval expeditions to Southeast Asia.

name: Delhi Sultanate
description: Turko-Afghan rule over north India. Qutb Minar. Delhi as Islamic cultural center. Timur's invasion devastated the capital.
politics: Military monarchy with iqta land grants

name: Vijayanagara Empire
description: Hindu empire in south India. Hampi capital. Resistance to Delhi Sultanate and Bahmanis. Portuguese trade contacts.

name: Mughal Empire
description: Turko-Mongol empire over most of India. Taj Mahal. Akbar's syncretism. Declined after Aurangzeb. British took over after 1857.

name: Maratha Empire
description: Hindu empire founded by Shivaji. Confederacy of Maratha chiefs under Peshwas. Fought Mughals, Afghans, and British.
politics: Confederacy of military chiefs under Peshwa

name: Sikh Empire
description: Punjab-based empire under Maharaja Ranjit Singh. Modernized army. Fell to British after Ranjit Singh's death.

name: British Raj
description: British Crown rule over India. Railways, telegraph, and civil service. Indian National Congress. Partition and independence in 1947.

name: Funan
description: Early mainland Southeast Asian polity in Mekong Delta. Indianized. Oc Eo port. Sanskrit inscriptions. Declined to Chenla.

name: Chenla
description: Khmer precursor state. Pre-Angkorian temples. Divided into Land and Water Chenla. Jayavarman II founded Angkor.

name: Khmer Empire
description: Angkor-based empire. Angkor Wat. Baray water system. Jayavarman VII. Thai and Vietnamese pressure caused decline.

name: Sukhothai Kingdom
description: First Thai kingdom. Ramkhamhaeng's Thai script. Theravada Buddhism. Absorbed by Ayutthaya.

name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
description: Siamese empire. Trade with China, Japan, Europe. Naresuan. Burmese conquest 1767.

name: Lan Na
description: Northern Thai kingdom. Chiang Mai capital. Mangrai. Silverwork and Buddhist scholarship. Burmese conquest.

name: Dai Viet
description: Independent Vietnamese state after Tang. Le Dynasty. Champa wars. Ming brief occupation 1407.

name: Champa
description: Indianized polity in central Vietnam. My Son temples. Rival of Dai Viet. Vietnamese annexation.

name: Majapahit
description: Javanese empire. Gajah Mada's palapa oath. Nusantara concept. Declined after Hayam Wuruk.

name: Srivijaya
description: Sumatra-based maritime empire. Palembang center. Buddhist. Rival of Java. Chola raid 1025.

name: Mataram Kingdom
description: Javanese kingdom. Sanjaya and Sailendra dynasties. Borobudur and Prambanan. Divided.

name: Malacca Sultanate
description: Malay maritime empire. Islam state religion. Melaka Strait trade. Portuguese conquest 1511.

name: Konbaung Dynasty
description: Burmese dynasty. Alaungpaya. Anglo-Burmese wars. British annexation 1885.
